co_half_half_crag.blurb: A small alcove of bolted lines in the Estes Park valley, high above Lily Lake and sharing a pocket with Woodstone and Slot Rock. Thirteen routes, nearly all sport with a single trad line, range from 5.8 up to the low 5.12s, and the bulk sit in the 5.10 range, so it suits climbers who are comfortable leading mid-grade bolted terrain. Many lines stay under 100 feet, though a few run closer to 130 feet and finish with a walk-off. The compact setting means a short day can still fit in plenty of pitches, and the walk in is a real uphill effort.
co_half_half_crag.parking_note: Leave the car at the overflow lot for Lily Lake, off the highway near Estes Park.
co_half_half_crag.approach: A path through the woods and talus climbs from the Lily Lake overflow lot to the alcove between Woodstone and Half & Half; allow about half an hour or a little more going up, less coming down.

co_main_wall_13.blurb: The main face of Surgery Buttress in Glenwood Canyon, just east of Glenwood Springs. All thirteen routes are bolted single pitches on vertical limestone, mostly short, running from 5.9 into the low 5.12s with most of the difficulty clustered at 5.11. The wall picks up sun from midday until dusk, which makes it a popular pick when the canyon floor is cold. Expect a scrambly, exposed walk along a ledge to reach it, finishing at a belay ledge below the lines. It is a compact, fairly serious crag for confident sport leaders rather than a place for first outdoor leads.
co_main_wall_13.parking_note: Use the Bair Ranch rest area at I-70 exit 129 and cross beneath the interstate to the north side.
co_main_wall_13.approach: From the north side of the highway, go through a concrete drainage culvert, follow the climbers' trail to the east end of the cliff, then traverse west along a ledge to the far end, passing the cave before scrambling up the right side of the wall to the belay ledge.

co_holy_water_wall.blurb: A compact high-elevation crag west of Buena Vista along the Cottonwood Pass road, at roughly 10,000 feet. About a dozen lines mix bolted sport, trad and a top-rope or two, with grades from easy up through the low 5.11s and the heaviest concentration around 5.10 and 5.11. The granite offers thin, solid edges and some crack systems, so expect technical face moves on slabby ground. Afternoon sun reaches the wall, and thunderstorms are a recurring afternoon hazard at this altitude, so an early start is sensible. It is a quiet spot with a short, rocky walk from the road.

co_butcher_knife.blurb: A small teaching-style crag tucked into a canyon right in the town of Steamboat Springs, near the middle school. Most of the thirteen routes are top-rope setups, with two trad lines, and grades stretch from the 5.7 range through to the low 5.12s with a good share at 5.8 and 5.11. The cliffs are short but pleasant, with crack climbing, a central flake and a main face, and the walk from the park is brief. It is a handy place for an after-work session or for introducing newer climbers to rope work. Winter is a poor season for climbing here.

co_wolf_creek_pass_west_side.blurb: The western slope of Wolf Creek Pass holds some of the larger water-ice lines in the San Luis Valley region, starting a few miles down the highway and finishing just below Treasure Falls. All thirteen climbs here are ice, spanning WI3 to WI5, with the bulk at WI4, so it is more of a destination for confident ice leaders than for first-timers. Treasure Falls and Tasty Freeze are the headline lines, and the area also holds easier WI3 routes. Ice quality varies from season to season, so check recent reports before heading up.

co_shaft_the.blurb: A narrow corridor crag at Devil's Head in the South Platte, set between two fins and reached by a faint trail from the Zinn Overlook. Thirteen bolted sport routes run from the 5.10 range through the 5.12s, with the harder end well represented. The climbs are short by local standards, around 40 to 50 feet, on featured rock with solid edges and incut flakes, and the left side is the steeper, better half. The passage gets very little direct sun, so it stays cool on hot days and is mainly a summer destination.

co_weller_slab.blurb: A south-facing slab above Weller Campground on Independence Pass, mostly trad with a handful of bolted routes. The thirteen climbs range from about 5.7 to the low 5.12s, with a decent cluster in the 5.10s. The obvious right-facing dihedral is its signature feature, and the rock is solid with big views all around. Getting there means a talus slog that takes roughly half an hour and is harder than it looks. The pass road is a summer-only affair, and the south exposure can make the slab hot, so plan for shade or cloud cover.
